title: Multi-Model Rollout Hedge and Escrow Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook documents the operational strategy and step-by-step procedures to protect SLOs and preserve error budgets during multi-model rollouts (canary → ramp → GA) by using capacity hedges and an escrowed token budget. It codifies automated heuristics, manual escalation flows, and configuration primitives used by runtime routing and SRE tooling.

Scope: Applies to all staged model variant rollouts in hosted and Dedicated deployments that affect production inference paths (text generation, chat, and embeddings). Excludes offline batch training jobs.

Definitions and key concepts

- Hedge: Reserved capacity (compute or token-priority) allocated temporarily to absorb increased latency or error rates during rollout.
- Escrowed tokens: A protected subset of tenant tokens or request priority credits reserved to keep critical traffic on stable model variants if the new variant degrades.
- Confidence band: Statistical window (e.g., 95% CI) on latency/error metrics used to decide safe ramp steps.
- Annealing schedule: Gradual rollback or reduction plan for a route weight when SLOs are violated.

SLO and error budget policy for model rollouts

- Critical SLOs (per-route): 99th percentile latency <= 220 ms for short-generation endpoints; success rate >= 99.5% for request completion.
- Error budget policy: During active rollouts, reserve a minimum of 30% of the route-level error budget as escrow. If escrow falls below 10% of original budget, automated rollback is triggered.
- Rollout-safe thresholds (examples):
  - Canary pass: 99th-latency within baseline + 10% and error-rate delta <= 0.1 percentage points.
  - Ramp hold: metrics within baseline + 20% OR escrow > 25% of original budget.
  - Abort/rollback: sustained violation for 5m OR single severe spike (error-rate increase > 1.0 percentage point and p95 latency > baseline + 50%).

Capacity hedging strategy (high-level)

1) Pre-rollout:
   - Reserve a hedge pool equal to 20% of expected peak capacity for the affected route. Hedge can be implemented as pre-warmed GPU instances, burst credit tokens, or prioritized token lanes.
   - Create an escrow allocation for tenant-critical flows: tag tokens with escrow=true in routing metadata.
   - Run a short synthetic canary suite (2–10k synthetic tokens) against the variant to produce an initial performance baseline.

2) Canary:
   - Route 1–3% of production traffic to canary variant. Monitor for 15m for early regressions.
   - Keep hedge idle but available; do not consume escrow for canary unless canary shows regression.

3) Ramp:
   - Increase weight in increments (1%, 5%, 10%) based on confidence band passing and escrow level. After each increment, wait at least 10–30 minutes depending on footprint.
   - If metrics degrade but escrow remains > 25%, shift non-critical traffic into hedge lane and continue monitoring.

4) GA:
   - Once variant reaches intended weight and passes a 6–12 hour stable window, release hedge capacity and return escrow to normal accounting. Record metrics and create a retrospective entry.

Automated runbook: Hedge activation and escrow usage (detailed steps)

Triggering events (automated):
- A: route metric breach: p99 latency > threshold for 3 consecutive 60s windows.
- B: error-rate delta > 0.5 percentage points relative to baseline over 5m.
- C: escrow < configurable threshold (default 10% of original allocation).

Automated response sequence (system || SRE tooling):
1) Detect: metric aggregation service flags event A or B.
2) Pause ramp: rollout controller sets new_variant_weight = previous_weight.
3) Engage hedge: routing-controller marks <hedge_pool_id> active and instructs traffic broker to move non-critical requests to hedge lane.
4) Activate escrow policy: tag critical routes with escrow=true; ensure those requests continue to hit stable variant instances.
5) Notify: send automated pager duty event to oncall SRE with summary and playbook link.
6) Observe for 10 minutes:
   - If metrics recover within confidence band: de-escalate by draining hedge over 10 minutes and resume ramp at reduced step size.
   - If metrics do not recover: move to manual escalation.

Manual escalation and rollback procedure (SRE oncall)

1) Triage: open the rollout incident channel, attach the automated evidence bundle (latency histograms, error traces, model logs, kernel OOM or GPU saturation metrics).
2) Quick checks (first 5 min):
   - Is GPU utilization above 85% across the variant pool?
   - Are there signs of quantization quality regressions (spike in decode errors)?
   - Is there network or storage pressure (IOPS, underlying host errors)?
3) Immediate mitigations (choose in order until SLOs restored):
   - Route critical traffic to escrowed stable variant (set escrow=true override).
   - Scale up hedge pool by +15% capacity (if capacity available).
   - Cap token length or force p50 token-limit on canary traffic (temporary prompts truncation).
   - Rollback: set new_variant_weight = 0 and resume stable model.
4) Post-action verification: require 15 minutes of stable metrics after mitigation before closing the incident. If rollback performed, mark rollout failed and schedule a postmortem.

Escalation matrix and ownership

- Oncall SRE: initial triage and remedial actions (0–30 min).
- Runtime/Serving Lead: second-level (30–90 min) — investigate kernel regressions, quantization mismatches, autoscaler misbehavior.
- Model Owner (Product/Applied ML): notified at 30 min or on rollback — responsible for model-level fixes, dataset/ops regression.
- Infra/SRE Manager: invoked after 90 min for chronic capacity shortages or cross-service impacts.

Telemetry, evidence, and observability requirements

Minimum telemetry that must be attached to any hedge/escrow-triggered alert:
- Per-route percentile latencies (p50,p95,p99) at 10s granularity.
- Error-rate and error-class distribution (decode errors, timeout, OOM).
- GPU/GPU-memory utilization, host CPU, and i/o metrics for variant pool.
- Routing decisions log (per-request: model_version, lane, escrow flag, token length).
- Autotuner/quantization toggles and compilation flags for the variant.

Tooling snippets and example configs

1) Rollout controller excerpt (YAML):

controller:
  rollout_id: rollout-2026-11-modelX
  strategy: staged-weight
  steps: [1,5,10,25,50,100]
  confidence_window_minutes: 15
  hedge_pool: hedge-gpu-pool-a
  escrow_policy:
    percentage_reserved: 30
    trigger_rollback_threshold: 10

2) CLI: engage escrow override for critical-route

# mark route to use escrowed tokens-only
redwoodctl routes set-annotation --route critical-chat --annotation escrow=required --until 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z

3) Example alert rule (pseudo-sql):

WHEN p99_latency(route='chat-short', rolling=5m) > 220ms AND pct_change(error_rate, baseline, 5m) > 0.5 THEN TRIGGER HedgeActivate

Testing and rehearsal

- Weekly synthetic rollouts: run a simulated staged rollout in the staging cluster with the same hedge/escrow tooling. Validate that hedge activation, escrow tagging, and rollback paths execute without human intervention.
- Monthly chaos scenario: disable 20% of the stable pool during a simulated ramp and verify escrow retains critical traffic. Document gaps.

Postmortem and learning loop

- Any rollback or >30m incident during rollout requires a postmortem with the following sections: summary, timeline, evidence links, RCA, hypotheses tested, action items (owner + due date). Postmortems are required to be filed within 72h and reviewed by Runtime and SRE leads.
- Maintain a rollouts scoreboard: per-quarter success rate, median time-to-recovery, number of automated hedges engaged, escrow consumption metrics.

Appendix: configuration table (canonical defaults)

| config_key                         | default            | purpose |
|------------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
| hedge_pool_default_percent         | 20%                | fraction of peak reserved as hedge |
| escrow_reserve_percent             | 30%                | percent of error budget held in escrow during rollout |
| escrow_rollback_threshold_percent | 10%                | trigger rollback when escrow falls below this |
| canary_percent_default             | 2%                 | initial canary weight |
| confidence_window_minutes          | 15                 | wait time after each ramp step |
| max_ramp_step_percent              | 25%                | largest single ramp increment |
